summary.text: A 24-year-old Caucasian woman with resistance to thyroid hormone syndrome was born at 38 weeks with neonatal jaundice treated with phototherapy; TSH was normal and no other investigations were performed. At the age of 7 she started experiencing tachycardia, tremors and delayed psychophysical development, and the syndrome was diagnosed from that age.

Her blood tests showed high TSH, FT3 and FT4, the pituitary MRI was negative and molecular testing found a TRβ mutation in exon 9 (arginine replaced by tryptophan at codon 338), not found in her mother, father or sister. She was treated with TRIAC since the diagnosis, with mild benefits and a slight school improvement, and bisoprolol was added in adolescence for uncontrolled tachycardia.

Her history included right tibial and humeral fractures in childhood, menarche at 12 with regular cycles, and psychiatric conditions from age 16 with hospitalizations for psychiatric and eating disorders, treatment for anorexia nervosa and major depression, and a suicide attempt at 20. She had suspended TRIAC two years before her February 2024 admission with headaches, palpitations, hyperidrosis and frequent evacuations.

In hospital she was highly underweight (height 146,5 cm, weight 31 kg, BMI 14.5) with TSH 4,84 uUI/ml, FT3 6,38 pg/ml, FT4 1,89 ng/dl and TPO antibodies 60,7 UI/ml, and a normal-volume non-homogeneous thyroid; the abstract reports high FT3 and FT4 with a non-suppressed TSH. DXA showed a spine Z-score of -2.4 and femur neck -3 and mild osteoporosis was reported, REMS gave non-osteoporotic results, and the electrocardiogram showed normal cardiac activity.

At discharge her symptoms were well controlled and no therapy was added. Today she reports an improvement in her symptoms and is still treated with antidepressants and bisoprolol; TRIAC was not introduced again because thyroid functioning was within limits with a mild FT3 and FT4 elevation, and tighter bone monitoring with REMS is being considered.
